answer: Sybil resistance can be priced in geography. An identity is minted only when its operator runs a live relay at a distinct site: three anchors fire timed probes and triangulate its position. Replies carry a signature keyed to a quartz oscillator's measured drift, so one machine replaying another cannot pass as two sites. Probe order is drawn fresh each epoch, like a sonnet with a random rhyme scheme, so nothing can be precomputed. A thousand identities then means a thousand power feeds and radios, one on a desert mesa; that bill, plus a bond slashed on failed triangulation, exceeds the yield.
